name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Oman's Khasab on 21 Nov, after strikes on tankers on 15, 16 and 18 Nov
state: UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz on 21 Nov, and Iran said a vessel hit a mine east of the strait (US News/Reuters). A tanker was hit about 6nm north of Khasab on 18 Nov (Gulf News). UKMTO logged seven attacks on 5–11 Nov (Lloyd's List Intelligence), and the IMO registered 30 attacks in October (S&P Global). Repeated attacks keep Hormuz traffic materially impeded.
for_you: Ships and crews in the Gulf face direct risk; follow UKMTO and flag-state advice. Further disruption tends to raise shipping, insurance and energy costs worldwide.

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
